newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WATCH OUT FOR THOSE CURVES, BATTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WATCH OUT FOR THOSE CURVES, BATTER.

text.p: The Northern League St. Paul Saints announced its opening-day roster on Friday, including a 22-year-old left-handed relief pitcher with a nasty curveball and long brown hair.

Ila Borders, who has played with the boys since the age of 10 in her native California, will be the first woman ever to pitch on a men's professional baseball team. Women players have held other fielding positions on men's teams.
Borders gave up six runs in three innings of work in two exhibition games with the Saints but earned her roster spot, team officials said.
"She doesn't throw particularly hard, and her curveball is her best pitch," team public relations director Dave Wright said, adding, "she's cute and she's funny."
The Saints, who are not affiliated with a major league team, begin defence of their Northern League championship Friday night in Sioux Falls, South Dakota.

The 150-pound (68 kg) Borders will don her uniform in a seperate lockerroom at the Saints' quirky home field, where fans can get a haircut and a massage while watching a pig deliver spare balls to the umpire.
Last year, New York Yankees slugger Darryl Strawberry launched his comeback with the Saints, appearing in 29 games before being called up to help win a championship with the Bronx Bombers.
